## How to buy the best 1-inch air filter: Filtration, MERV, and lifespan explained

Fitting to the name, a 1-inch HVAC air filter measures one inch thick. Though this may seem thin, these filters are among the most popular because they can fit into tighter spaces while still adequately capturing dust, pollen, pet dander, lint, bacteria and other particles.

Read on to learn more about 1-inch air filters and how they contribute to clean indoor air and efficient furnace and air conditioner operation:

### Understanding 1-inch air filter performance

1-inch air filter performance is largely based on [MERV ratings](https://filterking.com/hvac-filters/merv-ratings), or minimum efficiency reporting value. Generally speaking, the higher the MERV rating, the more particles the filter can capture. For example, a [MERV 8 air filter](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-8) is ideal for general filtration and captures 90 percent of particles, while [MERV 11](https://filterking.com/hvac-filters/merv-11-air-filter-review) and [MERV 13](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-13) capture 95 percent and 98 percent of particles, respectively.

MERV 11 and MERV 13 are ideal in households with more allergy-sensitive residents. In addition to dust, pollen, mold, dust mites, bacteria and pet dander, MERV 11 filters also capture smoke and smog particles. MERV 13 air filters trap all of this, plus allergens. They also assist with odor elimination.

Another option is [MERV 8 carbon filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-8-carbon), which help eliminate odors from pets, cooking, smoke or other household chemicals.

Though they're an excellent air filter option in the right circumstances, 1-inch filters tend to have less surface area than thicker models, which can limit their ability to trap fine airborne particles. They can also be fast to dirty, requiring more regular replacement of such filters.

### Choosing the right 1-inch air filter for your needs

So, what's the best furnace and AC filter for your household? The best pick should balance your household's filtration needs and the capability of your HVAC unit.

Do this by matching the MERV rating on the filter to meet household members' needs. For instance, if residents are sensitive to allergens, choose a 1-inch filter with a higher MERV rating to ensure more dust, pollen and dander are filtered and don't circulate throughout your home. This results in healthier, cleaner air.

### When to consider other thicknesses

Thicker [2-inch](https://filterking.com/air-filter-sizes/2-inch-air-filter), [4-inch](https://filterking.com/air-filter-sizes/4-inch-air-filter) and [5-inch](https://filterking.com/air-filter-sizes/5-inch-air-filter) filter options are best suited for certain homes and situations. Thicker filters tend to work better in larger spaces, for property owners who want to extend filter product life, or homes with more allergy-sensitive residents or pets. Installing thicker filters can improve air filtration and extend filter lifespans.

However, it's important to ensure your HVAC unit is designed to handle a thicker filter. Refer to your HVAC manual for the recommended filter size and type or measure the media cabinet around the filter slot to help determine this.

### Maximizing your filter's lifespan

It's only natural to want to extend your HVAC filter lifespan to ensure you're not regularly replacing them. Some maintenance best practices to extend filter product lifespan include:

- **Select the right filter** to balance your household's needs and your HVAC unit's capability. Optimizing the product type, thickness and MERV rating has a direct impact on your filter's lifespan.
- **Maintain a clean home:** Regular dusting, sweeping, vacuuming and cleaning help reduce the amount of particles that circulate throughout the home and can become trapped in the filter.
- **Clean your ducts:** Aside from routine home cleaning, have your air ducts cleaned to remove the buildup of dirt, debris, pollen, lint, mold, bacteria and more. Buildup in ducts can also soil the air filter more quickly. According to the National Air Duct Cleaners Association, it's recommended that property owners have their ducts cleaned every three to five years.
- **Manage sources of pollution:** Activities such as cooking, smoking and running fireplaces can introduce pollutants to the home that can clog air filters faster than normal. Ensure you have proper ventilation to manage this.

### Signs it's time to replace your HVAC filter

How do you know when it's time to change your HVAC filter? There's a mix of performance indicators and HVAC unit warning signs that you should be paying attention to. Here's a closer look:

- **If it's dirty or clogged:** Remember to change your air filter at least once every 90 days. Properties with allergen-sensitive residents or multiple pets should consider changing them as often as every six weeks.
- **If there's reduced airflow when the furnace or cooling system is on:** Weak airflow from your property's vents may be a sign of a soiled filter. Reduced airflow can also lead to poor heating and cooling efficiency throughout your property.
- **If you and your family experience more allergic reactions,** it could be because fewer particles are being trapped. This means more dust, dander and pollen are circulating throughout your home and impacting indoor air quality.

Beyond air quality issues that may result in allergic reactions and increased medical costs, failing to adequately change your air filter can also put more strain on your HVAC unit. This can lead to higher heating and cooling costs and the need to have your unit serviced and repaired more routinely.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What size 1-inch air filter do I need?

Measure the size of your HVAC filter to determine its proper size. You can also check the dimensions of your current filter. Filter King carries a range of high-quality standard-size air filters and offers [custom-sized air filters](https://filterking.com/custom-air-filters) for HVAC systems with unique requirements.

### How often should I replace my 1-inch air filter?

Replace your 1-inch air filter at least once every three months. However, this frequency can differ based on your filter's MERV rating and other factors, like pets or residents sensitive to allergens. For instance, properties with residents sensitive to household dust and other allergens should change their filters as often as every 6 weeks. Consider Filter King's [bulk purchasing or subscription options](https://filterking.com/air-filter-delivery) to ensure you always have a clean air filter stocked and ready, while saving on price.

### Will a 1-inch filter fit my HVAC system?

Whether a 1-inch filter will fit your HVAC system depends on its housing, so it's important to know the exact dimensions required. Check the old filter to determine the proper length, width and thickness. Also, ensure that the filter fits snugly and is not too loose or too tight. Proper air filter fit is important to optimizing airflow and system efficiency.

### Can I use a 1-inch filter in a 2-inch slot (or vice versa)?

No, never use different [air filter sizes](https://filterking.com/air-filter-sizes), such as a 1-inch filter in a 2-inch slot. This will create a gap, thereby allowing unfiltered air to bypass the filter, reducing efficiency and restricting airflow. Restricted airflow can also lead to potential HVAC unit damage. You also shouldn't use a 2-inch filter in a 1-inch slot for similar reasons. It's important to find the right filter for your HVAC system to ensure proper airflow and system effectiveness.

### How do I measure for a 1-inch air filter?

Check for a 1-inch air filter by first turning off your HVAC system and removing the old air filter. From here, use a tape measurer to determine its dimensions (length, width and depth). Record the actual dimensions and then round up to the nearest whole inch to determine the nominal size. Shop for a new air filter by the nominal size.

### What's the difference between MERV 8, MERV 11 and MERV 13?

The biggest difference between MERV 8, MERV 11 and MERV 13 filters is the particle capture. [MERV 8 filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-8) trap 90 percent of common particles, while [MERV 11 filters](https://filterking.com/hvac-filters/merv-11-air-filter-review) capture 95 percent, and [MERV 13 filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-13) capture 98 percent. MERV 11 and MERV 13 are ideal in households with allergy-sensitive residents, while MERV 8 is better for general use. [MERV 8 carbon filters](https://filterking.com/air-filter/merv-8-carbon) are another option and help eliminate odors, such as those from pets, cooking, smoke or other household chemicals.

### Do 1-inch filters restrict airflow more than thicker filters?

When other factors like MERV rating and brand are the same, 1-inch air filters do not restrict airflow more than thicker filters do. If you do notice your 1-inch filter restricting airflow, consider switching to a model that features a lower MERV rating.

### Can I wash and reuse my 1-inch air filter?

No, most 1-inch air filters are disposable and cannot be washed and reused. Washing a dirty air filter will likely damage the material, making it less effective. It could also leave it damp and more susceptible to mold growth, which can further lead to poor air quality throughout your home. Only select air filters, such as electrostatic models, are designed for reuse.
